mainTopic: Who carries the burden of proof in a doubtful case: two reports of שמואל's rule, tested against the כלה משנה and the needle ברייתא
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a discussion about שמואל's ruling that, in a doubtful trade, the donkey owner must bring proof even though he holds the cow. The גמרא tests whether the משנה of a כלה found with blemishes really supports this. First the proof from כלה בבית אביה is challenged. Then רבי אבא's version from כלה בבית חמיה is challenged too. רב נחמן בר יצחק finally bases the proof on the father keeping the קידושין money, a proof that works according to all views. A ברייתא about a needle found in an animal's stomach then challenges שמואל, and the defense does not fit the ברייתא's general wording. So רמי בר יחזקאל rejects his brother יהודה's report and says שמואל's real rule is: whoever had possession when the doubt arose must bring proof. The needle ברייתא is challenged against this rule as well, and it is explained as a butcher who already paid, since normally no one hands over an animal before payment. The amud ends by turning to the חכמים's view that the משנה's rule applies only to hidden blemishes, introducing a statement of רב נחמן.

steps.title: The case of a bride in her father's house is not comparable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks שמואל's proof. In the case of a כלה בבית אביה, the father brings proof in order to take money away from the husband. In the donkey case, the donkey owner brings proof in order to keep what he already holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the case of a bride still in her father's house really comparable? There, the father brings proof in order to take money out of the husband's hands. Here, the owner of the donkey brings proof in order to keep what he already has.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the proof that שמואל brought from the כלה בבית אביה case and says the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כלה case, the father has to bring proof because he wants to take the כתובה money from the husband, and the one who takes money from another always needs proof. The donkey owner is already holding the cow, so he is keeping, not taking. That makes it harder to see why he should need proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A bride who is betrothed but still living in her father's house
Is it comparable? (a challenge to a proof)
Takes money out of another person's possession
Keeps, maintains what he already holds
The owner of the donkey

steps.confusionAlert: The text starts mid-discussion. 'הָתָם' (there) is the כלה case from the משנה, and 'הָכָא' (here) is שמואל's case of the cow traded for a donkey.

phrases.english: A bride in her father's house — is it comparable?
phrases.notes: This is the case from the משנה where a כלה is found with blemishes and her father must bring proof.

phrases.english: There, the father brings proof and takes out money,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא — מַיְיתֵי בַּעַל הַחֲמוֹר רְאָיָה וּמוֹקֵים.
phrases.english: here, the owner of the donkey brings proof and keeps.
phrases.notes: He keeps the cow that he already holds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's proof, which was made before this section begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's proof from כלה בבית אביה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father is taking money (מוציא), while the donkey owner is keeping it (מוחזק). A rule that requires proof from a taker cannot prove that a holder needs proof.

steps.title: רבי אבא: the proof is from a bride in her father-in-law's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא moves the proof to the case where the כלה has already entered her husband's home. There the husband, who holds the money, must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: the proof is from a bride who is already in her father-in-law's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא repairs the proof by pointing to a different part of the משנה, where the husband must bring proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is in the husband's home, the husband must prove the blemishes were there before the קידושין. The husband is the one holding the money, since he does not want to pay. So here the holder needs proof, just like the donkey owner.

keyTerms.meaning: A bride who has entered her father-in-law's (husband's) home

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
A bride in her father-in-law's house.
phrases.notes: Meaning she has already entered the husband's home, and in that case the husband must bring the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: כַּלָּה בְּבֵית חָמִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by choosing a case where the holder is the one who brings proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-sourcing the proof to a different case in the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof came from the father, who takes money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof comes from the husband, who holds the money and still must bring proof.

steps.title: Still not comparable: the husband breaks a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא. The husband needs proof because he is fighting the father's חזקה. The donkey owner's proof actually supports the חזקה that is already on his side.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is still not comparable. There, the husband brings proof and weakens the father's חזקה. Here, the donkey owner brings proof and keeps the חזקה in his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבי אבא's version too, because the husband's position is weaker than the donkey owner's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's proof goes against a חזקה that favors the father, so it makes sense that he needs proof. The donkey owner's proof matches the חזקה about the donkey's body, and he also holds the cow. With both on his side, why should he need proof?

keyTerms.meaning: And still, even so
A presumption about the status of something
Weakens, undermines
In his hand, in his possession

phrases.english: And it is still not comparable:
there, the husband brings proof
and undermines the father's presumption,
phrases.notes: This is the presumption about the girl's body, which works in the father's favor.

phrases.english: here, the owner of the donkey brings proof
and keeps the presumption in his hand.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's proof from כלה בבית חמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband needs proof because he is going against a חזקה. The donkey owner has the חזקה on his side, so the cases are different.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the proof is from the קידושין money
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the proof is from a כלה בבית אביה, but about the קידושין money. The father holds that money, and he still must bring proof to keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the proof is from a bride in her father's house, regarding the betrothal money.
steps.whatsHappening: A third version of the proof is offered, now focused on the קידושין money instead of the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blemishes were there before the קידושין, the קידושין was a mistake and the husband wants his money back. The father is holding that money, yet he must bring proof to keep it. That is exactly like the donkey owner who holds the cow and still needs proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal; here, the money given to make the betrothal

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
A bride in her father's house, and regarding the betrothal money.
phrases.notes: The proof isn't about the כתובה, but about whether the father keeps the קידושין money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כַּלָּה בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ, וּלְקִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problems raised in steps 1 and 3 with a new angle on the כלה בבית אביה case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-sourcing the proof to a different kind of money in the same case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof was about the כתובה, where the father is the one taking money.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the קידושין money the father is the holder, and he still must bring proof.

steps.title: The proof works even for the view that קידושין money is given to be lost
steps.stepSummary: The proof does not depend on the dispute about whether קידושין money must be returned. Even the view that it is 'given to be lost' says so only about a certain קידושין. A mistaken קידושין is different, so the father keeps the money only with proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say this works only for the one who holds that betrothal money was not given to be lost. Even the one who holds that betrothal money was given to be lost means only a definite betrothal. With a mistaken betrothal, if the father brings proof, yes, he keeps it. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof is being protected from a possible objection, showing it holds according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the father returns the money only according to the view that קידושין money is not 'given to be lost'. But even the other view applies only to a real, certain קידושין. A קידושין that may have been a mistake never really took effect, so the father, though holding the money, must prove his claim. That fully supports שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Given to be lost; once given, it is not returned
A betrothal that definitely took effect
A mistaken betrothal
And do not say
According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: The final proof for שמואל: a father holding קידושין money from a possibly mistaken קידושין keeps it only if he brings proof. So even the one holding the item needs proof in this kind of doubt, and this is true according to all views.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes שמואל's rule stand on its own, without depending on the dispute about returning קידושין money.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Given to be lost' is about a valid קידושין that later ends. It does not apply to a קידושין that was a mistake from the start.

phrases.english: And do not say this is only according to the one who says
betrothal money was not given to be lost.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'given to be sunk.' This view holds the money comes back if the betrothal ends.

phrases.english: Rather, even according to the one who says
betrothal money was given to be lost —
this applies only to a certain betrothal,
but with a mistaken betrothal,
if he brings proof, yes,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the father, who is holding the money.

phrases.english: if not, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 4 by showing it does not depend on a dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the other view to certain קידושין so the proof works for all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof might work only for the view that קידושין money must be returned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the view that קידושין money is given to be lost agrees that with a mistaken קידושין the father keeps the money only with proof.

steps.title: A teaching about a needle found in an animal's stomach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a needle in the stomach wall. When there is no scab over the wound, the timing is unknown and the claimant must bring proof. A butcher who already paid must prove his claim to get his money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A needle is found in the thick wall of the second stomach. If it went through one side, the animal is kosher. If it went through both sides, it is a טריפה. If a drop of blood is found on it, we know it happened before the slaughter. If no blood is found, we know it happened after the slaughter. If a scab formed over the wound, we know it happened three days before the slaughter. If no scab formed, the one who wants to take money from his friend must bring proof. So if the butcher already paid, he must bring proof, and then he can take his money back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a ברייתא to set up a challenge against שמואל. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key case is the wound with no scab. We cannot tell whether the damage happened before the sale or after it. In that case the butcher who already paid is the one trying to take money out, so he must bring proof, even though the seller is the one holding the money.

keyTerms.meaning: The second stomach of an animal
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten
A scab formed over the wound
The one who wants to take money from another must bring proof

steps.confusionAlert: The blood and scab details are only background. The part that matters for שמואל is the last line: the butcher who already paid must bring proof.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: a needle that is found
in the thick wall of the second stomach,
if it went through one side, the animal is kosher.
If it went through both sides, it is a treifa.
phrases.notes: Both sides means the needle made a hole all the way through the stomach wall.

phrases.english: If a drop of blood is found on it,
it is certain that it happened before the slaughter,
if no drop of blood is found on it,
it is certain that it happened after the slaughter.
If a scab formed over the wound,
it is certain that it happened three days before the slaughter.
If no scab formed over the wound,
the one who takes money from his friend must bring the proof.
And if the butcher already gave the money,
he needs to bring proof, and then he takes it out.
phrases.notes: He means the butcher can take his money back from the seller only after proving his claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כלה cases are settled, the גמרא brings a new source that seems to argue against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the donkey owner must bring proof even though he holds the cow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this ברייתא the person holding the money, the seller, does not have to bring proof. The burden falls on the butcher who wants to take money out.

steps.title: Why doesn't the animal's owner have to bring proof?
steps.stepSummary: Following שמואל, the seller holding the money should have to prove the sale was good. Why does the ברייתא put the burden on the butcher?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let the owner of the animal bring proof and keep the sale standing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its question directly. According to שמואל, the seller should be the one who brings proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's donkey case, the donkey owner already held the cow and still had to bring proof to keep it. Here the seller holds the butcher's money, so by the same logic he should have to prove the sale. The ברייתא instead puts the burden on the butcher, which seems to go against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: But why? A challenge to a stated ruling
The owner of the animal, here the seller
And let him keep it standing, so the sale holds

phrases.english: But why?
Let the owner of the animal bring proof and keep it standing!
phrases.notes: This follows שמואל's donkey case, where the person holding the item still had to bring proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? בַּעַל בְּהֵמָה לַיְיתֵי רְאָיָה וְנוֹקֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא from step 6 into a direct challenge against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling, which puts the burden of proof on the butcher who already paid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to שמואל, the side holding the money should still have to prove his case, so here the seller should bring proof.

steps.title: The butcher had not paid yet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a butcher who has not paid yet. That makes the seller the one claiming money, so the seller must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the butcher had not yet given the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by limiting the ברייתא to a butcher who had not paid yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the butcher has not paid, the seller is the one trying to collect money. So 'the one who takes money from his friend must bring proof' means the seller. That fits שמואל and removes the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he did not give
The butcher

phrases.english: It is where the butcher had not given the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא was about a butcher who already paid, which would make the person holding the money free from bringing proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a butcher who has not paid. The seller is the one claiming money, so he must bring proof, just as שמואל would say.

steps.title: But the teaching gives no such limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The ברייתא states its rule with no limits, so it seems to cover a butcher who already paid too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was it stated without any limit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The ברייתא never says it is only about a butcher who hasn't paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the one who takes money from his friend must bring proof' are general. They sound like they apply whether or not the butcher paid. So limiting the ברייתא to an unpaid butcher does not fit its wording, and the challenge against שמואל comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it stated without any limit? An objection that a source speaks generally

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never answers this question directly. In the next step it gives up on יהודה's version of שמואל and brings רמי בר יחזקאל's version instead.

phrases.english: Why was it stated without any limit?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא doesn't say 'only if the butcher hasn't paid,' so how can we read that limit into it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 8 because it does not match the general wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about a butcher who has not paid yet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states the burden of proof in general terms. This suggests it covers every case, including a butcher who already paid, and that brings back the contradiction with שמואל.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל gives the true version of שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל says to ignore the rules his brother יהודה reported in שמואל's name. The real rule of שמואל is that whoever had the item when the doubt arose carries the burden of proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רמי בר יחזקאל came, he said: Do not listen to these rules that my brother יהודה stated in the name of שמואל. This is what שמואל really said: whoever had the item when the doubt came about must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenges against יהודה's version of שמואל were too strong. So the גמרא throws out that version and brings a different report of what שמואל actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the burden of proof depended on who held the money. Now it depends on whose possession the item was in when the doubt arose. Whoever had it at that moment must prove his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is being dropped.
Do not listen to them
Rules, general principles
The doubt arose while the item was in his possession

steps.whatToRemember: Under רמי בר יחזקאל's version of שמואל, the key question is whose possession the item was in when the doubt arose. That person must bring proof.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean שמואל changed his mind. Two students reported him differently, and the גמרא now accepts רמי בר יחזקאל's report over יהודה's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This replaces the rule the גמרא has been defending since the start of this section. Every challenge from here on is measured against this new version.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל, אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, when Rami bar Yechezkel came, he said:
Do not listen to these rules
that my brother Yehuda formulated in the name of Shmuel.
This is what Shmuel said:
Anyone in whose possession the doubt arose,
the burden of proof is on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל, אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in Step 9, the גמרא abandons יהודה's report of שמואל and brings a different one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever had the item in his possession when the doubt arose must bring proof.

steps.title: The משנה about a bride supports this rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's case of a כלה teaches the same idea. Whoever's possession she was in when the doubt arose must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא also taught the same idea in the case of a כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our own משנה already follows this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, if the blemishes are found while the כלה is still in her father's possession, the father must bring proof. If she has entered her husband's possession, the husband must bring proof. That is exactly 'whoever had possession when the doubt arose carries the burden.'

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the משנה) also taught this
A bride

phrases.english: And our Tanna also taught [this] regarding a bride.
phrases.notes: This points back to our משנה: in the father's possession the father proves, and in the husband's possession the husband proves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רמי בר יחזקאל's version of שמואל from the משנה itself.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that whoever had possession when the doubt arose carries the burden of proof
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of a כלה with blemishes, in her father's possession or her husband's

steps.title: The needle case seems to contradict the new rule
steps.stepSummary: In the needle ברייתא, if the טבח has not paid, the animal's owner must bring proof. But the doubt arose while the animal was with the טבח, so the טבח should carry the burden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: A needle found in the thick wall of the second stomach, and so on. And if the טבח had not paid, the animal's owner must bring proof before he can collect. But why? The doubt arose in the טבח's possession!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the needle ברייתא to challenge רמי בר יחזקאל's version of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was slaughtered and found טריפה while it was with the טבח. So the doubt arose in his possession. Under the new rule the טבח should have to prove, yet the ברייתא puts the burden on the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal's second stomach
The animal's owner, here the seller
And collects (takes the money out)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַחַט שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת בְּעוֹבִי בֵּית הַכּוֹסוֹת כּוּ׳,
phrases.english: A needle found in the thick wall of the second stomach, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא quoted back in Step 6.

phrases.english: and if the butcher had not paid the money,

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל בְּהֵמָה בָּעֵי לְאֵיתוֹיֵי רְאָיָה וּמַפֵּיק,
phrases.english: the animal's owner must bring proof, and then he collects.
But why?
The doubt arose in the butcher's possession!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new version of שמואל from Step 10 using the ברייתא from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר יחזקאל's version of שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubt arose with the טבח, so he should carry the burden. The ברייתא instead places it on the owner when the טבח has not paid.

steps.title: The ברייתא means the butcher already paid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where the טבח already paid. Then the טבח is the one asking for money back, and he must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about where the טבח already paid the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא as a case where the טבח had already paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the טבח already paid, he is the one asking for his money back, and the ברייתא makes him bring proof. That fits the new rule, because the doubt arose while the animal was in his possession. So the ברייתא's rule is read as talking about a טבח who paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Who gave, who already paid

phrases.english: Where the butcher had paid the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by defining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא puts the burden on the owner even though the doubt arose with the טבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's main case is a טבח who already paid. He must prove, which matches the rule that whoever had possession when the doubt arose carries the burden.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא state it without limits?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can assume the ברייתא means a טבח who paid, when it states its rule with no limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what makes it so clear-cut?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own answer. Why would the ברייתא speak only about a טבח who already paid without saying so?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer that limits a ברייתא to one case needs a reason. The גמרא asks why that case would be the plain, assumed meaning of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What makes it clear-cut? Why state it flatly?

phrases.english: But why is it stated without qualification?
phrases.notes: Literally 'what is decisive?' He means: how can the ברייתא speak flatly, as if the טבח always paid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא refers to a טבח who already paid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives no sign that it means only a case where payment was made.

steps.title: Normally no one hands over an animal before payment
steps.stepSummary: In the ordinary case, a seller does not give the animal until he is paid. So the ברייתא can simply assume the טבח paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The usual way things work is that as long as a person has not paid money, the other person does not give him the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא did not need to spell out that the טבח paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since sellers normally require payment first, a טבח who is slaughtering the animal has almost always paid. So the ברייתא's plain case is a טבח who paid, and the new rule of שמואל stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The ordinary situation, the usual way
Coins, money
An animal

steps.whatToRemember: The needle ברייתא is read as a case where the טבח already paid, because that is the normal practice. This fits רמי בר יחזקאל's version of שמואל.

phrases.english: The ordinary situation is:
as long as a person has not given the money,
a person does not give the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 and supports the answer in Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא would need to say outright that the טבח paid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Payment before handing over the animal is the norm, so the ברייתא can assume it without saying so.

steps.title: The חכמים limit the rule to hidden blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה: the rule applies only to hidden blemishes. It then introduces a statement of רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: When is this said? With hidden blemishes. רב נחמן said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, the view of the חכמים, and begins to bring רב נחמן's comment on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים limit the husband's claim to blemishes he could not have seen. Visible blemishes are a different case. The words 'רב נחמן said' are a setup, and his statement comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say
In what case is this said?
Hidden blemishes

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
In what case is this said?
With hidden blemishes.
Rav Nachman said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא moves from the burden-of-proof discussion to the חכמים's line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the claim about blemishes applies only to hidden blemishes.
